body.p: Applicant has reviewed the Office action dated March 1, 2021, and the references cited therein. Claims 1-16 are currently pending. Claims 1-13 currently stand rejected. Claims 14-16 are withdrawn from consideration.
Applicant's Amendments

Applicant, in response to the objection to FIG. 5, has amended the specification (the paragraph at page 15, lines 24-30) to remedy the absence of the reference number "42" in the specification (as opposed to deleting the drawing the reference number from the drawing).

Applicant, in response to the grounds for rejection, has clarified the previously presented claims. Applicant has specifically amended claims 4, 7 and 8 to address the clarity-based rejections at pages 3-4 of the Office action. In the case of claim 7, Applicant deleted the specific example of the recited broader terminology. Claims 11 and 12 are clarified by using the well- established Markush claim construct.
No claim amendments were necessitated by the prior art-based rejections.
Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the grounds for rejection of the

previously pending claims in view of Applicant's further amendments to the claims and remarks addressing the shortcomings of the prior art with regard to particular recited elements of the claimed invention.
Please charge any fee deficiencies to Deposit Account No. 12-1216. Grounds for Rejecting the Claims

1. Claims 4 and 7-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. G 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. G112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §G112, the applicant), regards as the invention.
2. Claims 1-4, 11 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Derkx, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0360329 (Derkx) in view of Tupin, U.S. Pub. No. 2011/0060215 (Tupin).
3. Claims 5-6 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §G103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of McGrane, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0019988 (McGrane).
4. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. G 103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Maesani, U.S. Pub. No. 20 17/0273590 (Maesani).
5. Claims 8 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §G103 as being unpatentable over the
combined teachings of Derkx, Tupin and Maesani as applied to claim 7, and in further view of Muccio, U.S. Pub. No. 2012/0016440 (Muccio).
6. Claim 9 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §G103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Hsiao, U.S. Pub. No. 20 12/0265025 (Hsiao).
7. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Sims, U.S. Pub. No. 2007/029378 1 (Sims).
Applicant traverses the grounds for each and every rejection for at least the reasons set forth herein below. Applicant addresses the specific rejections in the order they arise in the Office Action.
Applicant's Specific Responses to the Grounds for Rejection
1. Rejection of Claims 4 and 7-10 as being indefinite

Applicant, in view of the corrective/clarifying amendments to claims 4, 7 and 8, traverses the rejection of claims 4 and 7-10 as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter of the invention.
2. Rejection of Claims 1-4, 11 and 13 as being obvious over Derkx in view of Tupin

arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes, ... wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are arranged for receiving electric physiologic signals..., wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes comprise one or more first electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso of the body, wherein the carrier further comprises at least one second electrode in addition to the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode being arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body, and to be aligned with the one or more first electrodes, ... for enabling electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm.

Moreover, the Office action does not establish a proper reason for one skilled in the art to modify Derkx's teachings, in view of Tupin, in a way that would result in Applicant's claimed invention. Notably, none of the references demonstrates any awareness of a particularized problem that would provide a reason to modify Derkx (in view of Tupin) in a way that resulted in Applicant's claimed invention.
a. Applicant's Claimed Invention
Applicant's claimed invention is directed to an arrangement that uses a carrier to hold a plurality of electrodes on a patient's body. In particular claim 1, provided in clean form below, recites:
A wearable device for monitoring one or more vital signs of a human
body, the device comprising:
a carrier suitable for being worn around an abdominal part of the body;
and
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes,
wherein the electrodes are arranged on the carrier to be brought in contact with a
skin of the body in use, and wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are arranged for receiving electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling
monitoring of a membrane potential of one or more muscles in the body,
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes comprise one or more first
electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso of the body, to receive via said first electrodes a first electrical signal indicative of a
membrane potential of a thoracic diaphragm of the body;
wherein the carrier further comprises at least one second electrode in
addition to the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode
being arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a mid front part of the
abdominal part of the body, and to be aligned with the one or more first
electrodes, the at least one second electrode thereby being arranged for receiving
a second electrical signal indicative of one or more further electric physiologic
signals from the body, for enabling filtering of the first electrical signal using the
second electrical signalfor enabling electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm.

Thus, Applicant's claimed invention provides a sensor arrangement that is uniquely arranged for monitoring respiration activity of pre-term born babies. See Applicant's Specification, page 1, lines 14-22. In stark contrast to using adhesive-mounted patches, in accordance with Applicant's claimed invention, a carrier is placed around a patient's abdomen that holds multiple electrodes in place. See Applicant's Specification, at page 2, lines 4-11. Per Applicant's disclosed/claimed invention, the carrier is suitable to be worn around the abdominal part of the body, and the carrier can be worn like a belt. See page 4, lines 11-19.
A technical difficulty arises from using a carrier, in place of adhesive patches (per

Derkx), the presence of a higher contact impedance - and hence weaker signals. In particular, the electric physiological signal from the thoracic diaphragm is very weak and distorted by many other signals from the body (see 2/13-2/20). Per Applicant's claimed invention, in order to enable an EMG to be provided, an improved signal-to-noise ratio is needed to provide a reliable measurement. See Applicant's Specification, at page 2, lines 18-20. Applicant's claimed invention overcomes the aforementioned technical problem by the at least one second electrode that provides a signal for filtering the first electrical signal.

The claimed filtering of the first electrical signal using the signal of the second electrode is described extensively by Applicant's specification at page 3, line 21 to page 4, line 19. Applicant's claimed filtering of the first electrode signal using the second electrode results in a signal having a higher SNR. The higher SNR, in turn, enables using the claimed carrier instead of a patch (per Derkx). The second electrode furthermore enables obtaining an ECG of the patient.
b. The teachings of the cited References
Neither Derkx nor Tupin particularly focusses on the challenges of monitoring preterm babies, and neither teaches or suggests Applicant's claimed solution thereto.
Derkx, upon which the Office action primarily relies, describes an adhesive patch placed upon a patient that holds a sensor in place upon a patient's body. The Office action, at page 4,
references FIG. 1, element 42 with respect to Applicant's "carrier suitable for being worn around an abdominal part of the body." FIG. 1 is reproduced below for convenient reference.
Moreover, Derkx does not describe Applicant's claimed "electrode arrangement

comprising a plurality of electrodes." Emphasis added. In Derkx, the patch includes only a single electrode 44 - with element 40 being an accelerometer that is not an electrode). Thus, the Office action on page 4 (at section 5), erroneously asserts that paragraph [0021] of Derkx describes "the patch has two electrodes arranged in it. " Applicant notes that FIG. 2 illustratively depicts details of the patch 42. In that regard, the detailed view of FIG. 2 unequivocally shows the patch includes ONLY a single electrode 44. See Derkx, para. [0064]. Paragraph [0021] refers to multiple electrode patches to be placed in several locations on the body, and not to a single patch covering all these places.
Furthermore, Derkx does not describe a single carrier that allows "one or more first

electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso" while also enabling "at least one second electrode being arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body ", while further enabling the second electrode "to be aligned
with the one or more first electrodes." There is no reason for such a carrier configuration in Derkx, which is based on patches 42 that can be adhered at any desired location on the body.
Lastly, Derkx also does not describe filtering of the first electric signal by using the second electric signal.

Moreover, the Office action, at page 5, concedes that Derkx does not describe a sensor arrangement for "enabling electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm." The Office action relies upon Tupin to fill admitted gaps in the teachings of Derkx regarding "enabling electromyography of the thoracic diagram." Tupin describes an ultra-wideband medical radar module (UWBMR) is described that transmit an electromagnetic signal S into the body to a target area T, using transmission antenna 30. See Tupin, FIG. 4 and paragraphs [0145] through [0148]. A reflected signal S' is picked up with a receiver antenna 40 that can be analyzed. The electrodes thus do not measure electric physiological signals, in particular not a membrane potential of one or more muscles. Tupin thus does not enable EMG, and for that reason alone already cannot be combined with Derkx as it is based on a different measurement principle.

However, Tupin does not describe an arrangement of multiple electrodes including first electrodes "in contact with a side part of a torso" and second electrodes "in contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body", wherein "the first electrical signal [can be filtered] using the second electrical signal for enabling electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm". Such filtering is not present since, in Tupin, the sensors appear to be operating in stand-alone manner.
c. The Combined teachings of the cited references do not render the claimed invention
Applicant, for at least the reasons provided above (specifically addressing the points

raised in the Office action), traverses the rejection of independent claim 1. As noted specifically above, neither reference describes several elements of the claimed invention. Importantly, Derkx uses patches that obviate any need to incorporate several elements of Applicant's claimed invention that are particularly useful for a "carrier" based arrangement - as opposed to a "patch" based arrangement for holding sensors to a patient's body to take appropriate readings. As such, there is no indication of a particularized problem in either cited reference that would lead one skilled in the art to modify Derkx in a way that resulted in Applicant's claimed invention.
d. The dependent claims are not rendered obvious by the cited references' teachings

Claims 2-4, 11 and 13 variously depend from independent claim 1, and incorporate each of the elements discussed herein above that are neither described nor suggested in Derkx or Tupin. Applicant traverses the rejection of dependent claims 2-4, 11 and 13 for at least the reasons discussed above with reference to claim 1.

Applicant reserves the right to provide additional reasons for distinguishing claims 2-4, 11 and 13 from the teachings of the prior art in the event that any further Office action recites new grounds for rejecting claim 2-4, 11 and 13, or any claim from which claims 2-4, 11 and 13 depend.
